entries.source_title: Chaque/Tous les + [durée] = Each/every + [duration] (French Indefinite Adjectives)
entries.note: The interval explanation was sound; added a distinction between calendar frequency and repeated event triggers, including standalone à chaque fois.

entries.source_title: Même can mean "same", "itself", "very", "exact" and "precise" as an adjective, and "even" as an adverb in French
entries.note: Existing teaching distinguishes agreeing same/exact/self from invariable even, including polite singular vous-même; the different roles already have constrained application.

entries.source_title: Dernier = final/previous (French Adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.note: Added recent periods, latest without finality and the preceding occasion to the existing final-versus-previous contrast, with context-dependent decisions.

entries.source_title: Forming the feminine of adjectives ending in -u in French
entries.note: Added the missing pronounced-gu feminine branch with full forms and both diaeresis spellings; retained ordinary -u agreement instead of extending the exceptional spelling to every -u adjective.

references.purpose: Verify the pronounced-u spelling branch and the equal validity of traditional and rectified diaeresis positions.

entries.source_title: Ancien = former/old (French Adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.note: Former status versus the age of an object is already contextualized and assessed; the wording avoids encouraging ancien as the ordinary adjective for an elderly person.

entries.source_title: Certain = specific / sure in French (adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.note: The existing specified-but-unnamed versus assured-result contrast includes agreement and a contextual meaning check; no missing decision step was found.

entries.source_title: Better and better, worse and worse = de mieux en mieux, de pire en pire (Comparisons in French)
entries.note: Existing gradual-change patterns were sufficient; added the fixed deterioration expression with pis and separated evaluative reactions from literal progression.

entries.source_title: Propre = own/clean (French Adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.note: Ownership, cleanliness and the separate propre à construction are already differentiated; position and plural agreement are tested without claiming that own implies clean.

entries.source_title: Plus... plus..., moins... moins... = the more...the more..., the less...the less... (comparisons with phrases)
entries.note: Paired complete clauses, mixed more/less relationships and the absence of an English-style article already support construction and interpretation; the lesson also avoids equating correlation with causation.

entries.source_title: Le/la/les plus and Le/la/les moins = The most and the least (Superlative with Adjectives in French)
entries.note: Ranking distinct members already includes article/adjective agreement, placement, comparison groups and possessive replacement; the tasks retrieve the relevant forms.

entries.source_title: Vrai = real/true (French Adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.note: The original distinction between emphatic genuineness and factual truth is contextual rather than a rigid translation rule; its contrasting tasks already require the intended reading.

entries.source_title: Supérieur à/Inférieur à (Irregular Comparatives in French)
entries.note: The existing decision uses adjective agreement and à with contractions, while excluding redundant plus in the ordinary direct comparison; no extra formation gap remained.

entries.source_title: Forming the plural of adjectives ending in -al in French
entries.note: The full masculine/feminine singular/plural pattern and independent -aux tasks already prevent confusing masculine plural with feminine -ales.

entries.source_title: Forming the plural of French adjectives ending in -al (exceptions)
entries.note: The published exception set has individual retrieval tasks, recognizes the historical sense of banaux, and already accepts both final, idéal and glacial plural variants.

entries.source_title: Meilleur, mieux, pire / plus mauvais, plus mal = better, best, worse and worst in French (irregular comparatives and superlatives)
entries.note: Added situational c'est mieux after être and a bon/bien reconstruction method; kept the existing complete meilleur agreement and worse/best distinctions.

entries.source_title: Cher= dear/expensive (French Adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.note: Affection, price and cher à as emotional attachment already have distinct examples and agreement tasks, avoiding a false rule that every post-noun cher concerns money.

entries.source_title: Quelque/quelques vs Un peu de/peu de = A couple/a few vs a bit of/few (French Indefinite Adjectives)
entries.note: Mass/count choice, the scarcity implication of peu, singular quelque temps and elision are already taught and assessed; quelques is correctly not restricted to exactly two.

entries.source_title: Compound colour names and colour names derived from things are invariable (French Colour Adjectives)
entries.note: Added noun-qualified shades and coordinated multicolour descriptions. Accepted agreeing as well as invariable coordinated adjectives for the same multicolour reading rather than importing an absolute invariability rule.

references.purpose: Check accepted agreement when each object carries multiple coordinated colours, rather than imposing invariability as the sole valid spelling.

entries.source_title: Some French adverbs end in -ément
entries.note: Added the absent uniformément in a material-distribution context with retrieval; the existing ten learned forms and warning against a universal -ément recipe remain.

entries.source_title: "Des" becomes " de/d' " in front of adjectives preceding nouns (French Articles)
entries.note: Added the necessary distinction between indefinite des and contracted de + les, with an introduction-versus-identified-reference contrast and tasks that preserve des where required.

entries.source_title: Animals names are often different for male, female and baby in French
entries.note: Added missing lion/deer wildlife families with articles, gender and a young-animal sex-versus-grammar contrast; preserved the extensive farm, pet and bird inventory.

entries.source_title: Passer/se passer/se passer de - the different meanings of the verb "passer" in French
entries.note: Added worked transferred-object/recipient roles, phone connection and an enjoyable time period, extending the existing route/event/doing-without explanations rather than merely listing more meanings.

entries.source_title: Differences between French and English usages - Passer un exam vs To pass an exam
entries.note: The exam tasks already distinguish participation from success and failure, and preserve the valid réussir à construction instead of making taking an exam imply a pass.

entries.source_title: Avoir un exam = To pass an exam (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.note: Extended contextual avoir result talk to an awarded qualification, contrasting that completed event with present possession or a scheduled exam.

entries.source_title: Passer can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Both six-person auxiliary patterns, subject agreement and time-as-direct-object analysis already support fair constrained keys; the published wording also acknowledges intransitive variation.

entries.source_title: Expressing "to leave" with partir/laisser/quitter/sortir in French
entries.note: The four leaving verbs already have full presents, complement patterns, temporary-versus-permanent cautions and the sortir auxiliary contrast, with distinct constructed tasks.

entries.source_title: Using the compound past (Le Passé Composé) vs the present (Le Présent) in negative sentences with "depuis" (since/for) in French
entries.note: Added a worked recent-start versus long-absence contrast for negative depuis longtemps, with explicit timeline evidence and a clearer positive depuis peu reformulation.

entries.source_title: Avoir du mal à/avec = To have trouble, to struggle to/with (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.note: The original à-infinitive versus avec-noun explanation, full avoir forms and difficulty-versus-pain contrast already have appropriate retrieval and application.

entries.source_title: Using "faillir + [infinitive]" to say you almost did something in French
entries.note: Added near-negative-event scope and the ordinary opposite outcome of faillir ne pas, plus object-pronoun ownership before the infinitive.

entries.source_title: Using "si" + L'Imparfait in hypothetical sentences with Le Conditionnel Présent
entries.note: Imagined present/future conditions, clause order, s'il and the contrast with open conditions are already worked; the no-conditional restriction is correctly limited to conditional if, not whether.

entries.source_title: Rappeler [à quelqu'un] = to remind [someone] in French
entries.note: Added three-role reconstruction for reminders and a genuine de-as-article contrast, preventing English of from being inserted before a remembered direct object.

entries.source_title: Qui = Who/which/that (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: Retained role-based qui/que selection and added worked reconstruction through adverbs and noun-subject inversion; an immediately following verb is not an absolute test for qui.

references.purpose: Verify that relative-clause subjects can follow their verbs, so immediate-next-word shortcuts cannot replace subject/object reconstruction.

entries.source_title: Que = Whom/which/that (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: Added que immediately followed by a verb and inverted noun subject, with agreement traced to the real subject; the next-word shortcut is explicitly subordinate to grammatical roles.

references.purpose: Verify that relative-clause subjects can follow their verbs, so immediate-next-word shortcuts cannot replace subject/object reconstruction.

entries.source_title: En can replace de + [phrase] (French Adverbial Pronouns)
entries.note: Preserved the valid personal-reference nuance and added quantity-of-people practice plus an unspecified-amount versus identified-object contrast; en is not categorically forbidden for people.

references.purpose: Check that en can refer to people, notably in quantity constructions, instead of importing a blanket prohibition.

entries.source_title: Using neuter pronouns le or l' to refer to previously mentioned ideas (French Direct Object Pronouns)
entries.note: The fact/adjective reprise was sound; added le faire to recall an entire action and a task that places neutral le beside its infinitive.

entries.source_title: Y can replace à + [thing/object/location] (French Adverbial Pronouns)
entries.note: Added a whole à-infinitive complement replaced by y. Kept the verb-sensitive distinction between lui/leur and à plus a stressed personal pronoun rather than treating all human à complements alike.

references.purpose: Verify penser à and its personal complements; an à complement referring to a person does not automatically become lui or leur.

entries.source_title: Celui/celle/ceux/celles = the one(s) (French Demonstrative Pronouns)
entries.note: All demonstrative-pronoun forms and their required specifying complements are already taught; exercises distinguish them from determiners and require gender/number selection.

entries.source_title: Certain(e)s d'entre eux/elles = Some of them (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.note: Subgroup pronouns already account for all-feminine versus mixed groups and for d'entre nous; the tasks test both selection and reference.

entries.source_title: Using French adverbial pronoun "y" in affirmative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif) in French
entries.note: The published imperative teaching already covers hyphens, linking s and all addressees, while guarding the case where y belongs to the following infinitive.

entries.source_title: Using French adverbial pronoun "en" in affirmative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif) in French
entries.note: Quantity retention, imperative order, moi/toi elision, aies-en and sers-t'en are already independently assessed; the next-infinitive exception is preserved.

entries.source_title: L'un(e) ... l'autre/Les un(e)s ... les autres = One ... the other(s) (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.note: The existing full paired-pronoun forms distinguish two referents, group subsets and reciprocal constructions with their needed prepositions; no extra formation gap remained.

entries.source_title: Using neuter pronoun le to replace adjectives (French Direct Object Pronouns)
entries.note: Neutral le already stays invariable across feminine/plural subjects, elides where required and is retrieved in adjective-state contrasts rather than mistaken for an agreeing noun pronoun.

entries.source_title: Où can mean where AND when (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: Added direct time-question quand versus noun-relative où, preserving the existing place/time role analysis and the deliberately constrained vivre exercise.

entries.source_title: Ce qui (vs ce que) = what/which (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: Extended unnamed-role reconstruction and distinguished finite clauses from quoi plus infinitive; ce qui is selected by the missing subject role, not the category of the immediately following word.

references.purpose: Verify that relative-clause subjects can follow their verbs, so immediate-next-word shortcuts cannot replace subject/object reconstruction.

entries.source_title: Ce que (vs ce qui) = what/which (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: Added an unnamed object before an inverted noun-subject clause and finite-versus-infinitive tasks; ce que can precede a verb without becoming ce qui.

references.purpose: Verify that relative-clause subjects can follow their verbs, so immediate-next-word shortcuts cannot replace subject/object reconstruction.

entries.source_title: Ne ... nulle part = Nowhere (French Negations)
entries.note: Nulle part placement, the absence of an extra place preposition and the standalone response are already explained with distinct compound-past and retrieval tasks.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas = Not - with reflexive verbs in compound tenses (French Negations)
entries.note: All reflexive negative compound forms are present, with agreement limits and auxiliary-centred placement; the existing tasks require both the pronoun and the negative frame.

entries.source_title: Position of French object and adverbial pronouns in negative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif) in French
entries.note: The negative-command slot order already contrasts with affirmative attachment, removes linking s where appropriate and is exercised through multi-pronoun transformations.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs in the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif) - negative commands
entries.note: Added both standard s'asseoir families in all three negative-command persons and a key accepting both tu variants, alongside the existing negative-order explanation.

entries.source_title: Personne ne ..., rien ne ... = No one, nothing (negation) in French
entries.note: The original subject/object contrast correctly locates personne and rien, requires singular verbs for these subjects and excludes an unnecessary pas; those decisions are already tested.

entries.source_title: Using restrictive ne … que to express only with compound tenses (French Negations)
entries.note: Added action-only restriction versus object restriction, including a clearer ne faire que plus infinitive reformulation and an intention-based choice task.

entries.source_title: Aucun/e … ne = None (French Negations)
entries.note: Added aucun/aucune d'entre eux/elles as a singular subject referring back to a plural group, with a worked agreement decision and constructed reply.

entries.source_title: Combining two or more negations (French Negations)
entries.note: Corrected the existing open never-again key to accept jamais plus as well as plus jamais; added explicit ordering nuance without implying that every negative combination is freely reorderable.

entries.source_title: Ni l'un(e) ni l'autre ne ... = Neither (one nor the other) (French Negations)
entries.note: Preserved context-sensitive agreement alternatives and added a standalone neither reply, showing why a verbless response has no ne.

entries.source_title: Omitting the "ne" in informal negative sentences in French (French Negations)
entries.note: Register-appropriate ne omission and restoration are already distinguished from losing the negative meaning; plus ambiguity and careful-writing expectations are explicit.

entries.source_title: Conjugate paraître/connaître and derivatives (+ avoir) - except apparaître and naître - in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Full connu/paru forms and the named derivative tasks already supply the needed past-family depth; publication être and rare rené remain carefully limited rather than universalized.

entries.source_title: Conjugate courir and derivatives (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Added concouru and encouru with contribution-versus-liability meanings and their different complement patterns, using the preserved full avoir paradigm.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs in the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif) - affirmative commands
entries.note: Added both complete affirmative s'asseoir command families and the separate pronoun ownership of aller plus a reflexive infinitive; tasks assess both variants and attachment.

entries.source_title: Conjugate battre and derivatives (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Added the missing rabattre branch in a practical folding-down use and a task requiring rabattu without spurious feminine subject agreement.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -er and -ir verbs in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: The full regular future patterns already retain silent written e, exclude present-tense -iss- and separate future tense from a simplistic distant-time rule.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: All six ser- forms, future states and the serai/saurai distinction are already visible and assessed; no extra stem instruction was needed.

entries.source_title: Conjugate avoir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: All six aur- forms already appear with future resources and avoir expressions, including a future time clause and targeted person retrieval.

entries.source_title: Conjugate faire in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: The complete fer- paradigm and practical future-action examples already support the person-specific construction tasks.

entries.source_title: Conjugate aller in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: All six ir- forms are already taught, with a movement-plus-infinitive context and a contrast from the near-future construction.

entries.source_title: Conjugate -dre and -re verbs in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: The remove-only-final-e decision is explicit and applied beyond one model; full attendre forms and named -re tasks prevent dropping a stem consonant.

entries.source_title: Quand/pendant que + future tense (Le Futur Simple) - not the present tense = When/while I do something in the future (Sequence of Tenses in French)
entries.note: Future time clauses are already contrasted with habitual present and conditional si, including overlapping events rather than only sequential ones.

entries.source_title: Conjugate -éXer, -eXer, -eter, -eler verbs in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: The existing named spelling branches, full forms and accepted traditional/rectified variants already provide deeper application than a single stem list; appeler/jeter exceptions remain explicit.

entries.source_title: Conjugate semi-regular -oyer/-ayer/-uyer verbs in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: The existing -oyer/-uyer versus -ayer distinction and variant keys are sufficient. Both retained-y and changed-i -ayer futures remain accepted in careful writing, not merely in speech or dialogue.

references.purpose: Confirm both -ayer future spellings are standard written forms, not alternatives restricted to speech or fictional dialogue.

entries.source_title: Conjugate venir/tenir and derivatives in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: Added parvenir, convenir, appartenir and contenir with full future forms and meaning-dependent complement choices, rather than extending the family through unsupported name-only examples.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vouloir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: The complete voudr- paradigm already distinguishes a predicted future wish from the polite conditional voudrais; the contextual items enforce that distinction.

entries.source_title: Conjugate pouvoir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: All six pourr- forms and the direct following infinitive are already worked in ability/opportunity contexts, with contrast from conditional possibility.

entries.source_title: Conjugate devoir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: The full devr- paradigm and obligation contexts already distinguish requirement from desire or ability while acknowledging that devoir can express expectation.

entries.source_title: Conjugate voir/envoyer in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: Voir/envoyer and the relevant derivatives already have complete forms and individual tasks; prévoir/pourvoir safeguards prevent applying verr- to every -voir verb.

entries.source_title: Conjugate recevoir and other -cevoir verbs in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: Added full reflexive s'apercevoir future forms and a worked glimpse-versus-realization contrast, including de before a noun versus que before a clause.

entries.source_title: Conjugate most French verbs in the conditional present (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.note: The future-stem plus imparfait-ending construction is already complete for regular and spelling-sensitive verbs, with hypothetical meaning and written future/conditional contrasts.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être in the conditional present in French (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.note: All six ser- conditional forms already support imagined states and softened requests; contextual retrieval goes beyond copying a single first-person form.

entries.source_title: Conjugate avoir in the conditional present in French (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.note: The complete aur- conditional pattern is already applied to imagined resources and a tentative request, with person endings independently retrieved.

entries.source_title: Conjugate pouvoir in the conditional present in French = could (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.note: The full pouvoir conditional already distinguishes a gentle request or possible option from past ability, and the tasks exercise both form and use.

entries.source_title: Conjugate devoir in the conditional present in French = should (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.note: The devoir conditional already separates advice from expectation and retains a direct infinitive; all persons and contextual advice tasks are present.

entries.source_title: Conjugate faire in the conditional present in French (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.note: The complete fer- conditional and practical imagined outcomes already provide both formation and meaningful use, so no additional repetitive person drill was added.

entries.source_title: Conjugate aller in the conditional present in French (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.note: All six aller conditional forms, including irions/iriez, already appear with future contrasts and imagined movement; no missing formation branch was found.

entries.source_title: Conjugate savoir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: The full saur- future already covers knowing facts or how to do something and distinguishes saurai from serai in worked examples and constrained items.

entries.source_title: En + "-ant" = While/by + "-ing" in French (Gerund/Le Gérondif)
entries.note: Formation, three irregular participles, reflexive/negative placement, shared subjects and method/time/condition/concession already have original examples and assessments; further padding would not fill a real gap.

entries.source_title: Conjugate valoir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: The complete valoir present already separates worth from cost and explains worthwhile effort and impersonal advice, with practical interpretation and form tasks.

entries.source_title: Conjugate courir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: Full courr- forms and named derivatives already support the present/future double-r distinction and nonliteral recourir à applications.

entries.source_title: Conjugate mourir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: The complete meur-/mour- pattern already includes ordinary figurative usage and the distinction from transitive tuer, with both stem shapes assessed.

entries.source_title: Conjugate apparaître in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: The existing full être paradigm, agreement and explicitly constrained keys are appropriate. Contemporary être preference is retained without declaring attested avoir impossible or equally usual.

references.purpose: Verify contemporary preference for être while retaining attested avoir, rather than presenting equal frequency or banning an auxiliary.

entries.source_title: Conjugate acquérir and other irregular -QUÉRIR verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Added formal s'enquérir with complete reflexive forms and register-sensitive practice. Retained recognition-only old quérir rather than promoting it as an ordinary productive present-tense family member.

references.purpose: Check the old/defective status of quérir before deciding against treating it as an ordinary productive present-tense target.

entries.source_title: Which prepositions to use with celebration days - like Christmas - in French
entries.note: Added precise day expressions and Hanoucca/Aïd contexts. The chosen name's article is learned lexically, and calendar notices are not made to assume every festival is a single fixed-date day.

references.purpose: Check the lexical gender and naming of Aïd in an actual current dictionary entry; teach the festival expression with its article rather than creating one solely because of a vowel.

entries.source_title: Expressing distance in French with "à ... de ..." = (at) ... km from ... (French Prepositions)
entries.note: Measured distance, travel-time distance with an explicit mode, de contractions and d'ici already have clear examples and construction tasks.

entries.source_title: Quelque chose de + [adjectif] = Something [adjective] in French
entries.note: The masculine-singular quelque chose de construction, elision and contrast with feminine une chose are already taught and assessed, rather than relying on the gender of chose alone.

entries.source_title: Which prepositions to use with name days - like Saint Valentine's Day - in French
entries.note: Added an explicit le jour de la reformulation that preserves the festival's feminine article; existing saint-name spelling and Toussaint coverage remain intact.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the compound past (Le Passé Composé) in French - with nouns
entries.note: Extended noun inversion to coordinated groups containing moi or toi, with the required nous/vous auxiliary and repeated-subject choice.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions with reflexive verbs in the compound past (Le Passé Composé) in French
entries.note: Added role-by-role analysis of the two nous/vous occurrences in reflexive coordinated-subject questions, including agreement and a constructed inversion group.

entries.source_title: Expressing dimensions and measurements in French (French Numbers)
entries.note: Added agreeing être + dimension adjective + de against fixed measurement expressions, noun alternatives, and sur between side lengths without confusing them with area.

entries.source_title: Expressing fractions in French - general (French Numbers)
entries.note: Added singular/plural agreement alternatives for a singular fraction of a plural group and contrasted a genuinely singular amount; both valid group-agreement answers are accepted.
